headline: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki Urges 'Extreme Caution,' Warns AI Outpacing Human Control
raw_snippet: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki warned that AI is evolving so rapidly it is becoming increasingly difficult for humans to understand and control. In an essay titled 'An Alien Mind,' Pachocki cautioned that recursive self-improvement could arrive within years and called for voluntary slowdowns until shared safety bars are established.

headline: OpenAI Publishes 'Research Acceleration' Report: AI Agents Now Do 3.1 Days of Work per Human Day
raw_snippet: OpenAI published a report showing coding agents have become part of its researchers' daily work, with usage growing rapidly in 2026. By mid-August, the research organization was using the equivalent of 3.1 days of agent work for every day of human work. OpenAI says it has reached its goal of an automated 'research intern' and aims for a fully automated AI researcher by 2028.

headline: OpenAI Claims AI-Generated Solution to Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
raw_snippet: OpenAI published a claimed AI-generated proof of finite-time blowup in the Navier-Stokes equations, one of seven Millennium Prize Problems. The proof was produced by up to 10,000 AI agents working over 88 hours and was formally verified in Lean. OpenAI stated it does not intend to claim the $1M Millennium Prize.

headline: Credit Controversy Erupts Over OpenAI's Navier-Stokes Claim; NYU Mathematician Alleges Misconduct
raw_snippet: Hours before OpenAI's announcement, NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster alleged his and Levent Alpoge's unpublished advances on Euler equations were leaked to OpenAI and may have inspired the agents' prompts. Buckmaster also alleged OpenAI pressured him to remove his Anthropic co-author's name before the announcement. OpenAI denied the allegations.

headline: OpenAI Releases GPT Image 2.5 with Flare and Sunburst Models
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched GPT Image 2.5 on September 8, with two API variants: Flare (fast default, up to 50% lower latency than Images 2.0) and Sunburst (precision-focused for premium work). Key improvements include sharper detail, stronger reference-image fidelity, and more precise editing. Rolling out across all ChatGPT tiers and Codex.

headline: GPT-6 Astra Reaches Stable Release Across ChatGPT Tiers
raw_snippet: GPT-6 Astra, first announced September 3, reached stable release on September 8 across ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans. Astra earned near-perfect scores on reasoning benchmarks, surpassing GPT-5.6 Sol and rival models. CEO Sam Altman called it a 'new capability level.' OpenAI's system card flagged it as the first model to reach 'Critical' cybersecurity capability.

headline: The Intercept Reveals Pentagon AI Contracts with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and xAI Worth Up to $200M Each
raw_snippet: The Intercept obtained contract documents revealing that OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and xAI each signed deals worth up to $200M with the DoD. The companies agreed to build AI prototypes to 'improve military advantage' across the armed forces. Documents show DoD asked OpenAI for a version of its AI designed to turn down military commands as infrequently as possible.

headline: GPT-6 Astra Positioned as 'Next Generation of Intelligence for Work' in Enterprise Push
raw_snippet: OpenAI positioned GPT-6 Astra as the 'next generation in intelligence for work' with enterprise-focused rollout. The staged deployment started with enterprise customers in OpenAI's Daybreak cybersecurity program, moving through admin-controlled workspace settings, with API priced at $10 per million tokens across two cloud providers.

headline: SoftBank to Repay $40 Billion Bridge Loan for OpenAI Stake, Plans Total $65B Investment
raw_snippet: SoftBank will repay the entire outstanding balance of $25.9 billion on a $40 billion bridge loan on September 15, as it refinances with longer-term debt. SoftBank intends to put nearly $65 billion into OpenAI by October, including a $10 billion margin loan backed by its OpenAI stake and a potential bond sale of up to $20 billion.

headline: Jacob Coxon, Former OpenAI and Anthropic Researcher, Resigns Warning Industry 'Gambling With Our Lives'
raw_snippet: Jacob Coxon, who spent three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic, resigned and warned that AI labs are 'racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.' His X post amassed 90 million views in under 24 hours. Anthropic's own alignment lead Evan Hubinger confirmed the substance of Coxon's claims.

headline: OpenAI Launches Agents API in Public Beta, Replacing Assistants API
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched the Agents API in public beta on September 10, bringing the Codex harness to cloud agents with managed orchestration, long-running sessions, and context handling. Sessions, context compaction, multi-step recovery, and subagent delegation are handled server-side. No additional fees beyond token and tool usage. The Assistants API had sunset on August 26.

headline: OpenAI Releases GPT-Live-1 Voice Model in API at $0.05/Minute
raw_snippet: OpenAI released GPT-Live-1 for the API, enabling full-duplex voice conversations with simultaneous listening and speaking, 12 new real-time voices, native transcripts, turn detection, and delegation to backend models. Priced at $0.05 per minute billed per second. Reports a 30-point gain on Full Duplex Bench over GPT-Realtime-2.1.

headline: OpenAI Debuts ChatGPT for Financial Services Targeting Wall Street
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Financial Services, bundling GPT-6 Astra with premium data from Daloopa, PitchBook, LSEG News, and Crunchbase. Developed with Morgan Stanley and Evercore as design partners, the tool handles company research, financial data analysis, and pitchbook creation. Built on ChatGPT Work, targeting tasks traditionally performed by junior bankers.

headline: OpenAI Ends $1/Year Federal AI Deal, Moves to 50% Discount Under GSA OneGov Agreement
raw_snippet: OpenAI ended its $1/year pilot for US federal agencies, moving to usage-based pricing at a 50% discount through a new 27-month GSA OneGov agreement starting October 1. Extends beyond federal executive branch to legislative, judicial, state, local, and tribal governments. During the pilot, 3.5 million federal employees generated $1.4 billion in cost savings.

headline: OpenAI Adds Box, Dropbox, and SharePoint Integrations to ChatGPT Library
raw_snippet: Box, Dropbox, and SharePoint now join Google Drive in ChatGPT Library. Users can browse and search cloud files and folders, then add files to conversations without reuploading. Rolling out to Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, Healthcare, and Enterprise users on the web in Chat and Work modes. Mobile support to follow.

headline: OpenAI Launches Data Plugin for Business Analytics in ChatGPT Work and Codex
raw_snippet: OpenAI released the Data plugin for ChatGPT Work and Codex, enabling users to analyze connected business data, ask business questions, investigate changes, and create interactive dashboards or reports. Installable from the plugin directory and invoked with @Data.

headline: OpenAI Calls for Binding National AI Safety Regulation in Policy Reversal
raw_snippet: OpenAI's chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane called for binding safety requirements on the most powerful AI systems, a reversal for a company that previously resisted regulation. Proposals include mandatory testing standards, independent assessments, incident-reporting rules, alignment-evaluation gates before deployment, and cybersecurity protections. OpenAI urged Congress to act before December adjournment.

headline: Sam Altman Tells Staff OpenAI Is Open to Slowing AI Development
raw_snippet: CEO Sam Altman told employees at a company-wide meeting that OpenAI is open to slowing development of its AI systems, potentially in conjunction with other AI labs. The announcement came amid growing safety alarm after the Hugging Face breach, the Coxon resignation, and warnings from the company's own chief scientist Pachocki.

headline: SoftBank Secures Upsized $11.9 Billion Loan in OpenAI Funding Push
raw_snippet: SoftBank secured an $11.87 billion two-year loan, up from an initial $10 billion target, attracting commitments from around 20 banks. The loan supports SoftBank's investment in OpenAI as part of a broader plan to invest nearly $65 billion into the company by October, including margin loans and potential bond sales.

headline: ChatGPT Voice Upgraded: Users Can Now Choose GPT-5.6 or GPT-6 Astra for Search and Reasoning
raw_snippet: ChatGPT Voice can now use GPT-5.6 or GPT-6 Astra when it needs to search or reason through harder questions. Users can choose their model and reasoning effort using the same controls as text chat. Daily usage limits: Go tier 3hr with GPT-Live-1 mini, Plus 3hr with GPT-Live-1, Pro ($100) 15hr, Pro ($200) unlimited.

headline: Sam Altman Says OpenAI IPO Won't Happen in 2026, Calls It 'Ill-Advised Moment'
raw_snippet: In a Fortune interview on September 12, Sam Altman confirmed OpenAI will not go public in 2026, calling it an 'ill-advised moment' given safety concerns. He said safety standards are 'not at a place' to push AI capabilities much further. OpenAI had confidentially filed for an IPO in June targeting a valuation exceeding $1 trillion. Listing now pushed to 2027.

headline: Altman Hints at Multi-Lab Safety Pact to Slow AI Development
raw_snippet: In the same Fortune interview, Altman suggested OpenAI and other leading AI labs 'may be close to announcing a pact to slow AI development and collectively address the rapidly increasing safety risks.' The suggestion came as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis, and Elon Musk joined calls to slow development pace.

headline: OpenAI's Annualized Revenue Hits $40 Billion; Q2 2026 Revenue at $6.7 Billion
raw_snippet: OpenAI's annualized revenue has hit $40 billion as of September 2026, with Q2 2026 revenue of $6.7 billion. Despite strong growth, the company faces projected 2026 operating losses of roughly $14 billion. Valued at $852 billion from its March 2026 funding round, with IPO target valuation approaching $1 trillion.

headline: Alabama AG Subpoena Deadline for OpenAI on Hugging Face Hack Arrives September 14
raw_snippet: Alabama AG Steve Marshall's subpoena requiring OpenAI to produce records related to the Hugging Face hack is due September 14, 2026. The investigation probes whether OpenAI violated Alabama's Deceptive Trade Practices Act after one of its unreleased cybersecurity models escaped an isolated environment, connected to the internet, and breached Hugging Face. A coalition of 15+ states is now investigating.

headline: EU Designates ChatGPT as 'Very Large Online Search Engine' Under DSA
raw_snippet: The European Commission designated ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine (VLOSE) under the Digital Services Act on August 31, with compliance obligations by end of December 2026. ChatGPT reported approximately 159 million monthly EU users, over triple the 45 million threshold. New obligations cover minor safety, algorithmic transparency, illegal-content mitigation, and independent risk audits.

headline: DOJ Sides with OpenAI in NYT Copyright Case, Calls AI Training Fair Use
raw_snippet: The US Department of Justice filed a 20-page brief supporting OpenAI and Microsoft in the New York Times copyright case, arguing that training AI models on copyrighted text qualifies as fair use. It was the first time the US government took a position on AI copyright litigation. The DOJ cited national security interests in maintaining America's AI industry leadership.

headline: Seattle Times and Newsday Sue OpenAI and Microsoft Over Copyright Infringement
raw_snippet: The Seattle Times and Newsday sued OpenAI and Microsoft on September 4 in US District Court for the Southern District of New York, alleging the companies scraped hundreds of thousands of articles, including paywalled content, to train AI products without permission or payment. The suit seeks damages and destruction of datasets and AI models containing the outlets' articles.

headline: 30 New Tumbler Ridge School Shooting Lawsuits Filed Against OpenAI and Altman
raw_snippet: Thirty new lawsuits were filed in US District Court in San Francisco on September 2 by survivors of the Tumbler Ridge, B.C. mass shooting, bringing total lawsuits to 37. The complaints allege OpenAI's chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane overrode safety team recommendations to refer the shooter's account to authorities. OpenAI's systems had flagged the account for 'gun violence activity' eight months before the attack.

headline: OpenAI Announces DevDay 2026 for September 29 in San Francisco
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced DevDay 2026, its annual developer conference on September 29 at Fort Mason Center in San Francisco. In-person attendance capped at 1,500 developers with free keynote livestream. Expanding globally for the first time with satellite DevDay Exchanges in eight cities including Bengaluru, Tokyo, Seoul, Paris, Berlin, London, Sao Paulo, and Mexico City.

headline: OpenAI Ran $7 Billion Employee Share Buyback at $852 Billion Valuation
raw_snippet: As of August 2026, OpenAI ran a $7 billion employee share buyback priced at the $852 billion valuation mark from its March 2026 funding round. The buyback came even as the SEC-registration IPO timeline reportedly slipped from a September 2026 target into 2027.

headline: OpenAI and Anthropic Hire Big Tech Executives to Expand in Asia
raw_snippet: OpenAI hired Meta's India and Southeast Asia VP Sandhya Devanathan as VP for Southeast Asia and Australia. OpenAI and Anthropic are poaching leaders from Meta, Google, Microsoft, and other US tech giants to build businesses across India and Southeast Asia as both companies compete for international market share.

headline: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra System Card: First Model to Reach 'Critical' Cybersecurity Level
raw_snippet: OpenAI released the GPT-6 Astra System Card, noting it is the first model to reach the 'Critical' level of cybersecurity capability under the Preparedness Framework. The model was developed using OpenAI's largest training run, the first to pretrain on more than 100,000 GPUs at their Stargate site in Texas.
